questions.prompt: A CPU-percentage metric supports Average and Maximum at one-minute granularity. A chart averages each 30-minute interval, masking short spikes. You must inspect the highest collected value in each minute of the incident window. Which chart configuration meets the goal?

options.explanation: Each point reports the highest collected value in its one-minute interval.
Finer intervals help localize changes, but averaging does not preserve the highest sample in each interval.
It exposes a peak for each 30-minute interval rather than the required per-minute peaks.

options.text: Average aggregation; 30-minute time grain with a shorter displayed time range.
options.explanation: A shorter displayed range does not change the explicitly retained aggregation or interval size.

questions.prompt: An application metric exposes an Instance dimension with four worker values. All four workers have data in the selected window. You need four separate worker series on one Metrics explorer chart, without excluding any worker. Which configuration meets the goal?

options.text: Filter Instance to one worker without applying splitting.
options.explanation: This excludes three workers and does not display all four separate series.

options.text: Split by Instance and set the displayed-series limit to at least four.
options.explanation: Splitting creates one series per dimension value; the limit must include all four workers.

options.text: Filter Instance to all four workers without applying splitting.
options.explanation: The filter includes the workers but leaves their values combined into one series.

options.text: Split by Instance and set the displayed-series limit to one.
options.explanation: Splitting is appropriate, but the one-series limit omits three required workers.

questions.prompt: A metric records three values: 4, 6, and 10 in one interval. Which statement is correct when Count and Sum are supported?

options.explanation: Samples and total measured values are different quantities.
Average divides the sum by the sample count.
